# #647 — Automatic-capture liveness check: prove the raw capture lane delivered for recent sessions, loud on silence (replaces the retired capture merge-gate)

Ledger item 25 (docs/issue-graph.md): the capture merge-gate tier is retired — raw capture is automatic (Stop hooks → watermark → durable spool) and distillation is the DREAM pipeline's designed job (docs/dream-design.md). The enforcement that replaces it is LIVENESS on the automatic lane, the #625 pattern: a wedged or silently-dead capture pipeline must be loudly distinguishable from a healthy one.

Shape (delta on existing designs, not an invention): a deterministic check that recent sessions' capture events actually reached the server (or are sitting in the spool with the outage latch announced) — asserting on event counts/watermark advancement, NEVER wall-clock assertions (lane-contract round 5). Loud on: watermark not advancing while sessions run; spool accumulating with no outage latch; zero capture events across N recent active sessions. Control clause required: healthy path stays healthy (#624 clause-z / round-8 rule). Related: #646 (provider scope contradiction), #451 (hydration stamp + recall telemetry remain), #625 (the pattern's precedent).

### Direction taken and why — PR #648 body

> ## Summary
>
> - Closes #647 (ledger item 25). The capture merge-gate was retired because gating a human's PR is the wrong instrument for a background pipeline. This is the replacement: **liveness on the automatic lane**, the #625 pattern applied to the second background lane.
> - **This is not a new design — it is an existing one made executable.** `docs/decisions/capture-never-drops-a-turn.md` has specified the correct capture health check since 2026-07-28 (`:182-200`) and records at `:280` that "the check it asks for was never run". This PR runs it.
> - New `openbrain.apps.capture.liveness`: a **pure function over counts**. It opens no file, holds no lock, and takes no clock of its own. That shape is deliberate — `outage.py`'s module docstring records what happened the last time a capture-path component held a lock another waited on: a **healthy** hook stalled 31.4s, past the 5s Stop deadline, and the turn delivered zero batches ("the turn was DROPPED by its own telemetry"). A liveness reader that could do that would be strictly worse than the blindness it removes.
> - Three faults, all count-derived: watermark advancing **zero bytes while sessions run**; spool **accumulating with no outage announced** (`OutageLatch.note_spooled` returns `None` for three distinct reasons, so a latch that never fires is indistinguishable from a healthy one at the call site — `outage.py:411`); and any **role** delivering nothing.
> - **Per role is load-bearing, not decoration.** `capture-never-drops-a-turn.md:188-200` specifies it and explains why with a measurement: the operator's numbers stayed healthy for six days while the assistant side sat at zero (#447). On 2026-08-02 that was 365 user rows against 13 assistant rows — a lane-total counter reads 365 turns and reports busy traffic. Summing across roles rebuilds the exact blind spot this exists to remove.
> - `server/transport/health.ts` composes it exactly as `producerHealth` is composed (health.ts:129-134), **including the absence rule**: a process composing no capture lane publishes no block and stays green. Absent means "not my job"; `stale: true` means "my job and I am not doing it".
> - **No wall-clock assertion anywhere.** `silence_seconds` is reported and never compared (lane-contract Tightenings round 5).

> ## Critical Self-Review
>
> - Highest-risk behavior: a false-positive `stale` degrading `/health` on a healthy worker, since `/health` gates load balancing on core01's two workers. Mitigated structurally: absence and `undefined` both stay green (clauses f, f-health, f-health-undefined), and `MIN_SESSIONS_FOR_SILENCE = 2` keeps a single quiet session from tripping it (clause c-single). **No caller composes `captureHealth` in this PR**, so live blast radius is currently zero.
> - Assumptions that could be wrong: (1) that `sessions_observed` is a trustworthy denominator — the counter's *gatherer* is not built here, so a miscounting gatherer could manufacture either a false stale or a false green; (2) that role keys match `ob_raw_turns.role` values — asserted from the SQL at `capture-never-drops-a-turn.md:193-197`, not enforced by a shared enum; (3) that `MIN_SESSIONS_FOR_SILENCE = 2` is the right floor — chosen against the #447 evidence (a lane at literal zero for a full day), not tuned against a false-positive corpus.
> - Missing/weak tests: the reader has a done-means check and doctests but **no unit-test file** — deliberate, since the done-means driver exercises every branch through the shipped function and a second copy would drift. The gap that matters: **nothing tests the gatherer, because there is no gatherer** (see residual risk).
> - Security/permission risk: none identified. No namespace predicate, no ID-based read, no SQL, no auth surface. The reading is content-free by construction — counts, boolean flags, and role names only; `reason` carries no transcript text, path, or endpoint, matching the rule `outage.py`'s notices already follow.
> - Migration/deploy risk: none. No schema change, no migration. `captureHealth` is an optional input; every existing caller compiles and behaves identically (`tsc` clean, 3718 tests unchanged).
> - Downstream client/runtime risk: `SingleWorkerHealth` gains one **optional** field. Additive to a response body, so existing consumers are unaffected; `docs/downstream-rollout.md` classifies below — the block is absent on every process today.
> - Rollback/cleanup concern: revert is a clean two-file revert plus deleting one new module. No state is written, so nothing needs undoing.
> - Fixes made before PR: (1) **self-caught false-GREEN defect in my own driver** — an exception escaping `main()` left the TS driver exiting **0**, so a crashing subject would have banked a pass. Found while mutation-testing, not in any green run; fixed with an explicit `.catch` → `exit(1)` and **re-proven under the same mutation** (round-8: a repaired clause has never failed in its current form). (2) Removed an unused `Sequence` import ruff flagged.
> - Known residual risk: **the reading is WRITTEN, not RUNNING.** This PR builds the reader and the health composition; **no process composes `captureHealth` yet**, so no live `/health` reports capture today. That is deliberate scope — the gatherer must decide where per-session counts are aggregated across a fleet whose watermark and latch stores expose **no enumeration method** (`WatermarkStore` and `OutageLatch` are strictly single-key; confirmed by reading both). Designing that enumeration is a real decision, not a detail, and it belongs to its own lane rather than being invented silently here. Flagged for the decisions pass; the check proves the mechanism, not a live deployment.
